entries.note: Only explicit automation allocates the controls array. Record at most 512 visible control rectangles per rendered frame, preserving actual microui actions and tab/session identity. Ordinary widgets are clipped to their container. Upstream overflow scrollbar geometry is outside the content clip and is read directly from the container after mu_end_window; do not consult the popped clip stack there. Production rendering allocates none of this metadata. Tests use ordinary SDL pointer/wheel events to reach controls; they cannot bypass scrolling or call button handlers by name. Exported so owned view modules (formatview.c) register their controls without duplicating the clip arithmetic.

entries.note: A format-aware editor tab draws the mode toolbar first; text mode keeps the Save/Discard row below it and shifts the buffer down by one row, raw and text previews take the whole content area as a draw-list rect, and a tree preview lives inside the scrollable microui window with the selected entry drawn in the reserved lower split. Actions returned by the view are performed after drawing so request/mode changes never interleave with layout. The third root container per pane is avoided on purpose: the entry area is a draw-list rect, not another microui window (upstream's 32-root limit).

anchor.snippet: static void overlay_open(ReApp *a, mu_Context *ui, int kind) {

entries.note: Spec 080 decision 5 allows one overlay at a time, so the workspace holds one overlay kind and one anchor rather than a flag per surface. Opening a second surface cannot leave the first open, because there is nowhere to record that it was. Toggling is the same call, which is why the opener's own control closes it. An outside press closes the surface and then continues to whatever it landed on, so choosing another toolbar control takes one click rather than two; the opener's rectangle is excluded from that test, because otherwise the press would close the surface and the control's toggle would immediately reopen it.

A project root may carry a theme, and charter D34 is explicit that opening a repository must never change the workspace's appearance. The probe only reads the file's first line for its name, only when the settings popover is open, and only when the active root changed. Applying it takes a click, and the activation is remembered per root in the workspace preferences, so the trust decision is made once by a person rather than inferred from the contents of a checkout.

The view switcher is a fixed table walked by index, and the click handler branches on that same index — so inserting an entry is not a one-line change: `views` must match the table length and every later branch must be re-numbered. Devices was inserted at index 2, which moved the terminal/agent branch from `i == 3` to `i == 4`. Getting that wrong opens a shell where the user asked for an agent, silently, because both branches call launch_terminal. The group ring is drawn once around the whole run using GROUP_FIRST/LAST, so the first and last entries must stay first and last.

An external game runs in its own window, so its tab has no frame surface to draw: it shows the retained PTY output with a status row above it, and the row reads the session's live state rather than the tab's, because the process can exit while the tab stays open. The rect is still set from the game insets so the terminal below occupies the same area an embedded surface would. This branch must precede the t->game one — an external tab has a terminal and no game surface. Without it surface "external" has no view at all, which is what the vtmb-vr consumer declares for both of its games.

Pointer focus selects a view without changing its root/session binding. Toolbar focus clears custom editor/terminal/game keyboard routing. Detach never calls Stop. Wheel targets the visible hovered terminal/editor; negotiated terminal reporting gets first refusal before native history. Mouse motion/buttons route to an existing held terminal first, otherwise the hovered visible terminal; layout drags do not become application motion. Hover never changes keyboard focus. Focus loss releases all terminal holds, focus transfer releases the previous terminal, and hidden views release during drawing. Native UI still receives mouse motion to settle microui hover; consumed application buttons are not forwarded to chrome.
